findings.reason: without splitting, a case that fails on the gate half leaves the storage or sweep half unreviewed and unclosable, so the node cannot be marked done on one verdict.
findings.text: §71's Deliverable bundles four closable-in-their-own-right outcomes: a narrowed storage-failure rule, tests over three sweep sites, removal of a duplicate sweep helper, and a lander-composed landing carrying the run's passing gate — a reviewer cannot close the node on one verdict, and its one gate proves none of the four on its own

findings.reason: a deliverable with no case cannot be closed on evidence, and a single control over one deliverable leaves the other three unmeasured, which is the §69 defect this plan already has open against it.
findings.text: the deliverable requires "no duplicate sweep helper remains" but no done-when case measures that, and the sole negative control ("at the base revision, the first case fails: the test failure is read as a storage failure") exercises only the first of the four deliverables, leaving the helper-removal and passing-gate halves with no case that fails at base

findings.reason: a control that assumes an unstated §67 implementation may pass at base and prove nothing, and the finding asks the author to state the constraint against §67/§68's actual landed behaviour or move it into those sections.
findings.text: the opening grounds gaps 1–3 in behaviour no built code and no plan text states: "§67 matches storage phrases case-insensitively against every line of an arm's output" and "§68 sweeps leftover arm trees from three places" describe implementation neither §67 (plan.html:500-503) nor §68 (plan.html:507-510) specifies, and both sections are still `implementable` with no matching code in reckon/crew/landing_measure.py, so the negative control's "at the base revision … read as a storage failure" can only reproduce if §67 happened to be built that way

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited sections §57, §64 and §67 exist, the cross-plan reference `a-worker-or-its-job-cannot-overwrite-shared-files` resolves to docs/plans/a-worker-or-its-job-cannot-overwrite-shared-files.html, and the test path named is one the node will create.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the deliverable's third item ("no duplicate sweep helper remains") has no case in the done-when, and the single negative control measures only the first of four deliverables.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the base and head gate logs are named as sitting under the node's run directory, a durable path, not a node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section introduces no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into code; the test filename states the mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the opening states as fact that §67 matches storage phrases case-insensitively against every line and that §68 sweeps from three places, but neither section's plan text says this and neither is built (both still `implementable`), so the cited evidence cannot support the claim.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §71 carries four independent deliverables in one node (narrow storage recognition, test the three sweep sites, drop a duplicate helper, carry the run's passing gate into a lander-composed request).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §71 declares depends-on s67 and s68, which is where its first three gaps live, and it is added to §10's depends-on list and to the open followup f-dwl-s50, so the section is reachable and its upstream is declared.
